drug_class: CD4-directed post-attachment HIV-1 inhibitor (monoclonal antibody antiretroviral)
purpose: Ibalizumab-Uiyk is used to treat HIV-1 infection in adults who have tried many other HIV medications that are no longer working for them. It is used along with other HIV medicines as part of a combination treatment plan. This medicine is for people whose HIV virus has become resistant to multiple other treatments.
how_it_works: Your immune cells have a doorway on them called CD4 that HIV uses to sneak inside and take over. Ibalizumab is a special protein called an antibody that attaches to that doorway and blocks it, so HIV cannot get in. Think of it like putting a lock on the door so the virus cannot enter your cells and multiply.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, dizziness, nausea, and rash. Some people may notice changes in certain lab values like low white blood cell counts or high blood sugar. Most side effects are mild to moderate.
warnings: There is a risk of immune reconstitution syndrome, where your immune system starts recovering and may overreact to old infections already in your body, causing new symptoms. This medicine is given as an IV infusion, so tell your healthcare team right away if you have any reaction during or after the infusion such as chills, flushing, or trouble breathing. Do not skip doses, as missing doses can allow the virus to become resistant to the medication.
typical_dosing: Ibalizumab is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into a vein, usually in a clinic or infusion center. The usual starting dose is 2,000 mg given once, then 800 mg every 2 weeks after that. Your healthcare team will give you this infusion, so you do not need to inject it yourself at home.
